requirements.description: A single entry point states the phase, current Gate, latest checkpoint, and start protocol.
A Codex adapter binds the canonical contracts without adding independent policy.
A Claude Code adapter binds the same contracts.
Tool adapters stay semantically equivalent to the canonical roles.
The Gate sequence, dependencies, acceptance, and fail conditions are recorded.
The completion standard, mandatory controls, and Git and evidence discipline are recorded.
Tool-to-tool transfer is formal in both directions.
Checkpoint statuses, required events, required contents, commit semantics, and divergence handling are defined.
Done is defined and excludes assertion-only PASS.
Quality outcomes, required dimensions, and the promotion rule are defined.
Structural decisions are recorded as ADRs.
Architecture, roadmap, provenance, model usage, and detected tool capabilities are documented.
The canonical, tool-neutral role contracts exist, one per role of the delivery protocol.
Documentation, provenance, secret, tool-execution, and training-data policies exist.
Reusable templates exist for ADRs, checkpoints, gate reports, and handoffs.
Checkpoint state, run metadata, command, test, quality, provenance, and decision schemas exist and are loadable.
An experience schema is reserved for Gate 6 and implements no runtime.
Schema evolution is versioned and never invalidates a sealed checkpoint.
A checkpoint can be created with truthful non-PASS defaults.
A checkpoint can be finalized, and every finalization attempt is recorded with its exit code.
A checkpoint is validated against schemas, Git state, inventory, quality evidence, and secrets.
Secret redaction is available and documented to its real scope.
The tooling is standard-library only and portable across Windows and Unix-like checkouts.
Every checkpoint carries status, handoff, run metadata, state, plan, decisions, commands, file inventory, tests, quality, provenance, diff summary, risks, and next action.
`LATEST.md` points textually to the last checkpoint accepted by validation.
The file inventory matches the real change set, with bound content hashes.
Provenance is complete and `trainingAllowed` defaults to `false`.
A quality `PASS` carries resolvable evidence.
Handoff-ready and terminal checkpoints are anchored to an immutable namespaced tag.
A cold-start continuation prompt exists and depends only on checked-in files.
Cold-start validation is executed and recorded truthfully, including a blocked attempt.
Cross-tool validation state is structured and explicit.
A sealed checkpoint can be validated from a detached checkout of its own tag.
The handoff is executable by another tool without the producing session.
Every requirement of a delivery exists in a versioned matrix before implementation.
A Test Rework / Green Keeper role forbids shipping anything red and records every cycle.
A Delivery Completeness Validator audits the matrix before handoff and may not implement.
`GREEN_KEEPER_GATE` and `DELIVERY_COMPLETENESS_GATE` are preconditions of `READY_FOR_REVIEW`.
Readiness and blockage can never be claimed together.
Every operation attempt is recorded, including a refusal decided before execution.
Every recorded command is reproducible from its declared working directory.
The mandatory delivery order is stated in full in every governing document and both adapters.
The project keeps an organizational engineering memory of confirmed failures.
A lesson is `GUARDED` only when an automated control prevents recurrence.
A repeat increments recurrence, and a repeat against a guardrail is a `GUARDRAIL_FAILURE`.
A mandatory preflight selects the lessons that constrain each Gate.
Applicable lessons become requirements whose absence blocks completeness.
Lesson candidates can be extracted from recorded delivery evidence, never above `OBSERVED`.
External validation is grouped into milestones `M0` to `M6`.
An internal verdict is never described as independent external validation.
An extraordinary audit requires a recorded trigger.
Every completed Gate produces a retrospective.
One promotion invariant governs every positive terminal status, not only `READY_FOR_REVIEW`.
The mandatory quality gate set is a closed machine-readable registry that an invocation cannot narrow.
The expected requirement set is derived from canonical sources and compared exactly with the declared set.
An external milestone PASS is derived from an audit attestation authored by another sealed checkpoint.
A derived artifact carries a fingerprint of its inputs, and staleness is decided by recomputation.
Every lesson control, evidence path and provenance locator is resolved against the repository.
Every `GUARDED` lesson names a registered guardrail, and guardrail effectiveness is measured.
Sealed checkpoints are anchored by a hash-linked chain over tag, commit and tree.
Every count used as evidence is derived once and verified wherever a report states it.
Sealing is monotonic and post-commit, and every recorded command binds its declared inputs by content.
A milestone delivery carries an internal Red Team and an internal mirror audit, and neither is recorded as external validation.
Every finding of an independent audit is closed before the corrective delivery is offered.
A milestone verdict is carried by the audit checkpoint about a sealed subject, and its positive path is executed rather than only its refusals.
A generic guardrail derives repository state instead of naming a historical checkpoint, and the protocol's own next steps keep every mandatory gate green.
Every adversarial battery records a null-mutation control, and no count used as evidence is stated in prose.
An independent review is recorded.
An adversarial Red Team is recorded.
`GATE_PASS` is granted only by a run independent of the implementer.
No Gate 0 or later runtime is implemented during SETUP-00.
Documentation is maintained continuously rather than reconstructed at the end.
No secret, credential, or private chain-of-thought is stored.
Gate advancement requires explicit authorization and a passing previous Gate.
the external audit attestation can be written but never consumed, so `MILESTONE_EXTERNAL_PASS` is unreachable
a guardrail test is bound to a literal checkpoint name, so performing the protocol's own next step turns the mandatory `tests` gate red
a stale count survives in a current artifact because the count guardrail only inspects Markdown
a lesson's own note contradicts its status
a policy key is declared and never read
Defend attack A: Add a blocker to a READY_FOR_REVIEW checkpoint
Defend attack B: Set a review-ready quality dimension red
Defend attack C: Delete a canonical requirement and recompute every count
Defend attack D: Forge the stored counts of a passing report
Defend attack E: Remove a lesson-derived requirement from the matrix
Defend attack F: Replace a preventive control with documentation only
Defend attack G: Duplicate a lesson identifier
Defend attack H: Insert a secret-shaped value into a scanned field
Defend attack I: Rewrite a sealed predecessor, refresh hashes and move its tag
Defend attack J: Move a checkpoint tag and HEAD together
Defend attack K: Remove one inventory entry
Defend attack L: Silently modify a tracked file
Defend attack M: Set a wrong hashBefore
Defend attack N: Set a wrong hashAfter
Defend attack O: Claim PASS with no evidence
Defend attack P: Reference an unknown command
Defend attack Q: Supply complete attribution with empty evidence
Defend attack R: Promote an internally authored result to an external status
Defend attack S: Leave review and Red Team pending with a null auditor
Defend attack T: Request an audit without a known trigger
Defend attack U: Retire a canonical lesson but keep the active preflight
Defend attack V: Run the Green Keeper with an empty gate selection
Defend attack W: Claim PASS with a PARTIAL requirement
Defend attack X: Remove a required field from a command record
Defend attack Y: Point LATEST.md at an older checkpoint
Defend attack Z: Use path traversal as the Gate identifier
Verify checkpoint validation must succeed from a detached checkout of the checkpoint tag
Verify a file inventory must be recomputed from the repository, never trusted as an assertion
Verify every operation attempt must be auditable, including a refusal decided before execution
Verify a checkpoint may never claim readiness while it also claims to be blocked
Verify a PASS requires evidence that can be executed or resolved, not a statement
Verify the repository must be self-contained; a specification may not live outside it
Verify independent validation cannot be declared by the run that did the work
Verify requirement completeness must be total and evidence-backed before handoff
Verify a red gate requires rework, never a waiver, and never a weakened check
Verify a recorded command must carry runtime, working directory, commit and purpose to be replayable
Verify a control over a checkpoint's own evidence must be scoped to the moment it matters
Verify sealed checkpoints and their tags are immutable, and tooling must keep validating them
Verify an installed capability must be detected by resolved path, not by a bare command lookup
Verify evidence must be recorded as it happens, not reconstructed at the end of a run
Verify every positive terminal status needs one shared promotion invariant
Verify a mandatory set must be closed by policy, never chosen by the caller
Verify a completeness denominator must come from a source the delivery does not own
Verify a structured reference must be resolved, not merely well typed
Verify a derived artifact must carry a fingerprint of the inputs that produced it
Verify evidence produced from a dirty tree needs immutable input identity
Verify sealed history needs an anchor outside the content it describes
Verify an authoritative count must be derived once, never maintained by hand twice
Verify a lesson must cite a source that actually records the finding it claims
Verify a control is finished only when its positive path has been executed, not only its refusals
Verify a generic guardrail derives repository state instead of naming today's checkpoint
Verify an adversarial battery without a null-mutation control proves nothing
Verify a lesson's prose may record a residual limit but may never contradict its status
Verify a configuration key that no code reads is a defect, not documentation
Verify a required protocol transition must never turn a mandatory gate red
